review.title: Orchestration Persistence Foundation — Blind Review
review.head: 0395eaeaf5b9aadca9ee527bb3b6bd148fa94d9e
files_changed: tests/conftest.py (truncate list updated for new tables + upgrade-to-head)
review.summary: Sprint 005 Slice A is a well-structured persistence foundation. All five tables (job_definitions, schedules, runs, attempts, leases) are correctly created with explicitly named constraints, indexes, triggers, and FKs. The partial unique index for overlap prevention, the fencing token with monotonic increment trigger, terminal-state immutability trigger, and idempotency_key UNIQUE constraint all work as designed. No worker/API/frontend scope leakage. GuardianEvaluationRun model is unmodified. Migration downgrade only removes 0008 objects. 397 lines of PostgreSQL tests cover migration, schema, constraints, lifecycle, idempotency, overlap, fencing, and concurrency. Two MEDIUM findings warrant attention: (1) the idempotency key test formula uses full timestamp instead of date-only per Technical Design §8, and (2) attempts lack an immutability trigger despite the design specifying both runs and attempts should be append-only in terminal state. One MEDIUM schema deviation: runs.household_id is added without being in the Technical Design §6 schema. All other findings are LOW.

findings.title: fencing_token type deviation from Technical Design §6 (UUID vs INTEGER)
findings.description: Technical Design §6 specifies `fencing_token UUID NOT NULL` but the implementation uses `fencing_token INTEGER` with a monotonic-increment trigger. Technical Design §10 (Fencing Semantics) explicitly describes incrementing behavior ('Each lease claim atomically increments fencing_token'), which is incompatible with UUIDs. The implementation resolves the internal design contradiction correctly by choosing INTEGER.
findings.implementation_detail: Migration line 210: sa.Integer(), server_default=1; Trigger fn_lease_takeover_prevention does MAX+1 increment on INSERT
findings.why_not_blocker: INTEGER with monotonic increment is the semantically correct type for a fencing token. The design doc §10 explicitly describes incrementing — the §6 schema has a type error. This is a design document issue, not an implementation bug.
findings.recommendation: Update Technical Design §6 to specify `fencing_token INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` to match implementation reality and §10 semantics.

findings.title: runs.household_id column not in Technical Design §6 schema
findings.description: The `runs` table has a `household_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES household_profiles(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` column with named FK `fk_runs_household`. This column is NOT present in the Technical Design §6 schema for the `runs` table.
findings.implementation_detail: Migration lines 149, 160-163; ORM model lines 1170-1172; Both migration and model include household_id with FK to household_profiles
findings.why_medium: Adding a household_id FK to runs is functionally sound for the single-household model and consistent with existing patterns (all other tables are household-scoped). However, it is a schema deviation from the approved design that adds a FK not reviewed in the Technical Design.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) update Technical Design §6 to include household_id on runs, or (b) justify why the FK is needed (denormalization for query performance/household scoping) in a design addendum.

findings.title: Missing attempt immutability trigger — design specifies both runs and attempts should be append-only in terminal state
findings.description: Technical Design §6 states: 'Immutable triggers: runs and attempts are append-only after status reaches terminal state (completed, failed, aborted).' Only runs has `trg_run_immutability` via `fn_run_immutability()`. The `attempts` table has no equivalent trigger. An attempt in terminal state (succeeded/failed/aborted) can have its status freely modified.
findings.design_reference: §6 Recommended Schema — Immutable triggers paragraph after schema block
findings.implementation_detail: Migration: only trg_run_immutability is created (lines 177-183). No trigger on attempts. No fn_attempt_immutability function.
findings.why_medium: Without immutability enforcement on attempts, a bug could corrupt attempt history (e.g., changing a succeeded attempt to failed, or overwriting error_message on a terminal attempt). This is a database-enforceable constraint that the design explicitly called for.
findings.recommendation: Add an `fn_attempt_immutability()` trigger function and `trg_attempt_immutability` BEFORE UPDATE ON attempts that blocks status changes when OLD.status IN ('succeeded', 'failed', 'aborted'). Include a DELETE guard similar to runs. Add regression tests.

findings.title: Test idempotency key formula uses full timestamp, not date-only as specified in Technical Design §8
findings.description: Technical Design §8 states: 'Idempotency key formula: SHA256(job_type || canonical_job_params || scheduled_date).' The test helper `_idempotency_key()` uses `scheduled_at.isoformat()` (full ISO timestamp with time component) instead of extracting just the date portion. This means two runs for the same job on the same calendar date but at different times would produce different idempotency keys, defeating the daily dedup guarantee.
findings.implementation_detail: tests/test_orchestration_persistence.py lines 20-23: `payload = f'{job_type}||{scheduled_at.isoformat()}'` produces keys like 'guardian.evaluate_all||2026-07-18T09:00:00+00:00' instead of 'guardian.evaluate_all||2026-07-18'
findings.why_medium: If this helper formula is copied into the production worker in Slice B, daily deduplication will fail silently — multiple runs on the same day with different timestamps would all be accepted. The test should use the date-only formula to validate the design intent now.
findings.recommendation: Update `_idempotency_key()` to use `scheduled_at.date().isoformat()` instead of `scheduled_at.isoformat()`. Add a test that verifies two runs with different times on the same date produce the same idempotency key.

findings.title: No CHECK constraints on status columns for valid values
findings.description: Neither the `runs.status` nor `attempts.status` columns have CHECK constraints to enforce valid status values at the database level. The immutability trigger prevents transitions FROM terminal states but doesn't validate that inserted statuses are in the approved set.
findings.implementation_detail: Migration: status columns are plain sa.Text() with server_default. No CHECK constraint like ck_runs_status or ck_attempts_status.
findings.recommendation: Add CHECK constraints: `status IN ('pending', 'running', 'completed', 'failed', 'aborted')` on runs, and `status IN ('pending', 'running', 'succeeded', 'failed', 'aborted')` on attempts. This provides defense-in-depth against application bugs inserting invalid statuses.

findings.title: No CHECK constraint on attempt_number for positive values
findings.description: The `attempts.attempt_number` column is INTEGER NOT NULL but has no CHECK constraint to enforce `attempt_number >= 1`. A negative or zero attempt number could be inserted.
findings.design_reference: §5 Data Model Approaches — 'attempt_number tracked in attempts'
findings.implementation_detail: Migration line 192: `sa.Column('attempt_number', sa.Integer(), nullable=False)` — no CHECK constraint

findings.title: uq_schedules_one_per_job unique constraint not in Technical Design §6 schema
findings.description: The `schedules` table has `UNIQUE(job_definition_id)` named `uq_schedules_one_per_job`. This constraint is not present in the Technical Design §6 schema definition for schedules. It enforces one schedule per job definition, which is correct for Sprint 005's single-Guardian-consumer scope but would need to be relaxed if future sprints add multi-schedule-per-job-definition support.
findings.recommendation: Document this constraint in the Technical Design or note it as a Sprint 005 implementation decision. Consider whether multi-schedule support for a single job definition is a future requirement (if so, this constraint will need migration).

findings.title: fn_run_immutability allows updates to non-status fields on terminal runs
findings.description: The `fn_run_immutability` trigger only blocks status changes on terminal runs; it does not block updates to other fields (started_at, completed_at, triggered_by, etc.) on terminal runs. The Technical Design says runs are 'append-only after status reaches terminal state' but the trigger interprets this as status-immutable only.
findings.design_reference: §6 Recommended Schema — 'Immutable triggers: runs and attempts are append-only after status reaches terminal state'
findings.implementation_detail: Migration lines 28-31: Only checks `NEW.status <> OLD.status` for terminal states. Non-status field updates pass through.
findings.recommendation: MINOR: Consider whether non-status field updates on terminal runs should be blocked. If lenient interpretation is acceptable (allowing timestamps to be corrected), document this as an explicit decision. If strict append-only is desired, add checks for all mutable fields.

findings.title: Concurrency overlap test conflates partial unique index with idempotency_key constraint
findings.description: `test_concurrent_active_run_insertion` uses the same `_idempotency_key(...)` for both threads, meaning either the partial unique index OR the idempotency_key unique constraint could reject the second insert. The test cannot distinguish which constraint fired. However, the dedicated `test_overlap_one_active_run_per_schedule` test correctly uses different idempotency keys to isolate the partial unique index behavior.
findings.implementation_detail: tests/test_orchestration_persistence.py lines 360-397: Both threads compute `_idempotency_key('guardian.evaluate_all', now)` with the same `now` value
findings.recommendation: Update the concurrency test to use different idempotency keys (e.g., append a thread-specific suffix) to isolate and validate the partial unique index under concurrent load specifically.

verified_correct.detail: Partial unique index `uq_runs_one_active_per_schedule` on runs(schedule_id) WHERE status IN ('pending', 'running') correctly prevents two active runs for the same schedule. Tests validate serial and concurrent (threading.Barrier) enforcement.

Trigger `fn_lease_takeover_prevention` on INSERT computes MAX(fencing_token) + 1 per run_id with COALESCE for first lease. Trigger blocks direct UPDATE of fencing_token. Tests validate first-acquisition=1, takeover-after-delete, and immutability.

Schema provides heartbeat_at TIMESTAMPTZ, fencing_token INTEGER, and uq_leases_run. Token-gated heartbeat/finalize is application-layer (Slice B) via WHERE clause on fencing_token. Trigger guarantees token immutability. Schema correctly supports the design.
`fn_run_immutability` blocks UPDATE when OLD.status is terminal (completed/failed/aborted) and NEW.status differs. Blocks all DELETE. Tests validate revert-from-completed and deletion_forbidden.
schedules.enabled has server_default=FALSE in both migration (sa.text('false')) and ORM model (server_default=text('false')). Test validates default is False.

Downgrade drops triggers (IF EXISTS), partial index (IF EXISTS), tables in dependency order (leases→attempts→runs→schedules→job_definitions), then functions (IF EXISTS). Only 0008 objects removed. Alembic upgrade/downgrade/re-upgrade cycle clean.
Diff contains only persistence artifacts: migration 0008, 5 ORM models, and PostgreSQL tests. No worker process, API endpoints, frontend components, Guardian HTTP calls, or notification code.
runs.idempotency_key is TEXT NOT NULL with UNIQUE constraint named `uq_runs_idempotency_key` in both migration and ORM. Test validates duplicate rejection.
GuardianEvaluationRun model (lines 1055-1092) is unchanged from origin/main. New Sprint 005 models begin at line 1096 after a section separator comment. No diff touches GuardianEvaluationRun.

All 26 schema objects have explicit names: pk_job_definitions, fk_job_definitions_household, ix_job_definitions_household, pk_schedules, fk_schedules_job_definition, uq_schedules_one_per_job, pk_runs, uq_runs_idempotency_key, fk_runs_job_definition, fk_runs_schedule, fk_runs_household, ix_runs_job_definition, ix_runs_schedule, ix_runs_status, uq_runs_one_active_per_schedule, trg_run_immutability, pk_attempts, fk_attempts_run, uq_attempts_run_attempt, ix_attempts_run, pk_leases, fk_leases_run, uq_leases_run, ix_leases_worker, trg_lease_takeover_prevention, trg_job_definition_allowlist.

All columns, types, defaults, and nullable markers match Technical Design §6 with two noted deviations: (1) fencing_token: INTEGER instead of UUID (design doc internal contradiction — §10 describes incrementing; MEDIUM find H-1); (2) runs.household_id added (MEDIUM find M-1). All other aspects compliant.
Gate check report confirms 0001-0007 byte-identical vs origin/main. Test file HEAD_REVISION bumps are expected singleton-point changes.

`fn_job_definition_allowlist` fires BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE on job_definitions, rejecting any job_type not in ('guardian.evaluate_all', 'guardian.evaluate_one'). Tests validate rejection of 'shell.run' and acceptance of approved types.

All created_at, updated_at, scheduled_at, started_at, completed_at, acquired_at, expires_at, heartbeat_at, released_at, next_run_at columns use DateTime(timezone=True) in both migration and ORM model.

397 lines of PostgreSQL tests covering: migration head, job allowlist (accept/reject), schedule defaults (enabled=false, one-per-job), run lifecycle (terminal immutability, deletion forbidden), idempotency (unique constraint), overlap prevention (serial + concurrent with Barrier), lease fencing (first token=1, takeover token reset, token immutability), attempt uniqueness.
